title: Dense periodic behavior in surjective one-dimensional cellular automata
formal: For every finite nonempty alphabet A, radius r≥0 and local rule \(f:A^{2r+1}\to A\), let \(F:A^{\mathbb Z}\to A^{\mathbb Z}\) be defined by \(F(x)_i=f(x_{i-r},\ldots,x_{i+r})\). If F is surjective, must its temporally periodic configurations be dense in \(A^{\mathbb Z}\)?
definitions:
A configuration is a two-sided infinite sequence of letters. Give A the discrete topology and A^Z the product topology: specifying finitely many coordinates gives a basic open cylinder. Surjectivity means every configuration y has a preimage x with F(x)=y. Temporal periodicity means F^p(x)=x for some positive integer p, which may depend on x. Density means that every finite word u over A occurs, at coordinates 0 through |u|−1, in some temporally periodic x. This cylinder condition is equivalent to topological density.

The target does not require x to be periodic under spatial translation. Joint spatial and temporal periodicity is a stronger stated property and must not replace the requested condition without a proved implication. Eventual temporal periodicity also differs from periodicity from time zero. The full shift includes every A-valued sequence; no forbidden-word subshift, special algebraic alphabet or reversibility promise is imposed.
answer_criterion: Prove in Lean that every surjective local rule satisfies the cylinder condition, or give an explicit finite local rule, prove it is surjective, and exhibit a finite cylinder containing no temporally periodic configuration. Failure of spatial periodicity or of a particular period alone is insufficient.
context:
Boyle and Kitchens establish a positive result for closing maps while explicitly separating the unrestricted surjective case. Their theorem is not a theorem for every surjective rule.

Acerbi, Dennunzio and Formenti give equivalent formulations through changes of memory and related operations, helping delimit the conjecture’s scope.
why: The conjecture connects reversible coverage of configurations with recurrence in a basic discrete computation model.

import_provenance.original_title: Dense periodic behavior in surjective one-dimensional cellular automata
import_provenance.original_statement: Must every surjective cellular automaton on the full two-sided one-dimensional shift have a dense set of temporally periodic configurations? Equivalently, must every finite prescribed block occur in some configuration that returns to itself after finitely many updates?

sentences: A local rule updates every site of a two-sided infinite configuration.
Surjectivity guarantees a predecessor for every configuration.
The conjecture asks whether every finite observation extends to a temporally periodic configuration.
Spatial periodicity and eventual periodicity are different requirements.
